title: Transformer connections: primary-source review pilot
scope: All 22 canonical relationships incident to transformer. These supplemental reading notes are AI-assisted drafts, separate from the frozen canonical dataset and its evidence grades. Locators identify the portions actually inspected; abstract-only checks are not full-paper reviews. This is a bounded source pass, not a systematic literature or novelty search.

relationships.claim: The Transformer uses attention without recurrent sequence processing and explicitly relates its encoder-decoder attention to earlier translation attention.
relationships.limitation: This supports a specific architectural connection, not a complete history of attention.

relationships.claim: The original Transformer places layer normalization after residual connections around its sublayers.
relationships.limitation: This describes the 2017 architecture; later variants may place normalization differently.

relationships.claim: The Transformer paper compares its translation architecture against recurrent approaches and reports task-specific improvements.
relationships.limitation: These experiments do not establish universal supersession of LSTMs. Retain the legacy claim's limitation.

relationships.claim: BERT pretrains bidirectional Transformer representations and adapts them to language-understanding tasks.
relationships.limitation: Architecture reuse is supported; broader claims about priority or universal superiority are outside this note.

relationships.claim: GPT-2 uses a Transformer-based language-model architecture, with changes including normalization placement.
relationships.limitation: The source identifies reuse and modifications; it does not support every claim in the record's historical summary.

relationships.claim: Whisper uses an encoder-decoder Transformer for speech processing.
relationships.limitation: This checks the Whisper example only. The composite wav2vec-to-Whisper record needs separate evidence for each architecture.

relationships.claim: Switch Transformers combine sparse expert routing with Transformer language models based on T5.
relationships.limitation: This supports combining two traditions, not the claim that Transformers originated mixture-of-experts.

relationships.claim: Performers approximate Transformer attention using random-feature methods with linear sequence-length complexity.
relationships.limitation: This checks Performer, not every method grouped under the linear-attention record.

relationships.claim: Mamba evaluates selective state-space sequence models as an alternative to attention-based Transformer architectures.
relationships.limitation: Comparative motivation is not evidence that state-space models descend from Transformers or supersede them generally.

relationships.claim: Titans combines attention with a neural memory module intended to retain information beyond the immediate context.
relationships.limitation: This describes the paper's proposed architecture, not established general superiority or the entire test-time-learning field.

relationships.claim: The recorded research question concerns which data regimes and budgets favor deep tabular models over strong tree baselines.
relationships.limitation: A tabular benchmark supplies evaluation context, not evidence that this proposed combination is novel or solves the question.

relationships.claim: Decision Transformer frames offline reinforcement learning as conditional sequence modeling using a causally masked Transformer.
relationships.limitation: This supports one sequence-policy method, not an origin claim for offline reinforcement learning as a whole.

relationships.claim: Gato uses a decoder-only Transformer to model tokens from multiple tasks and modalities.
relationships.limitation: This architectural statement does not validate broad claims about mastery, abandonment, or general intelligence.

relationships.claim: RT-1 is a Robotics Transformer model trained on diverse real-robot data.
relationships.limitation: RT-1 is one example. Other systems grouped in the robot-foundation-model record need their own architecture and capability checks.

relationships.claim: The ROME study uses causal interventions to investigate factual associations inside autoregressive Transformer models.
relationships.limitation: This is a bounded example of model analysis, not a history or validation of all mechanistic interpretability.

relationships.claim: ROME modifies feed-forward weights to change selected factual associations in autoregressive Transformer language models.
relationships.limitation: The paper does not establish reliable editing for every model, claim, or activation-steering method.

relationships.claim: The exact relationship between the atlas's Transformer record and AlphaFold 2 requires a claim-specific architecture review.
relationships.limitation: The primary Nature article could not be retrieved during this pilot. No stronger claim or evidence upgrade is proposed.

relationships.claim: The broad Transformer-to-neuro-symbolic association needs a named method and a precise mechanism before it can be evaluated.
relationships.limitation: No claim-specific primary source was established in this bounded pilot. Keep the existing association visibly contextual.

relationships.claim: PagedAttention and vLLM address attention key-value-cache memory management during language-model serving.
relationships.limitation: This checks one serving technique, not every system or optimization grouped in the record.

relationships.claim: Kaplan and colleagues study empirical loss scaling, primarily in decoder-only Transformer language models.
relationships.limitation: These results are tied to the studied models and data; the composite Chinchilla record requires separate coverage.

relationships.claim: FlashAttention computes exact attention while reducing transfers between GPU memory levels.
relationships.limitation: The source supports an implementation improvement; it does not establish that approximate or linear-attention research became obsolete.

relationships.claim: Vision Transformer applies a Transformer to sequences of image patches for image classification.
relationships.limitation: The reported results depend on the paper's pretraining and evaluation setup; they do not establish that convolution is universally inferior.

steps.title: Start with alignment
steps.explanation: Translation attention lets a model use relevant parts of an input sentence. The Transformer changes how attention fits into the architecture.

steps.title: Inspect a component
steps.explanation: Layer normalization is explicitly named in the original Transformer. This is a concrete component relationship you can check in the paper.

steps.title: Read the architecture
steps.explanation: The 2017 model combines attention, feed-forward layers, residual connections, and normalization. Follow the source before generalizing from the map.

steps.title: Change the learning objective
steps.explanation: BERT uses bidirectional Transformer representations for language understanding. Reusing an architecture and changing its training objective are distinct choices.

steps.title: Change the input
steps.explanation: Vision Transformer represents an image as a sequence of patches. The source reports where that adaptation worked and under what training conditions.

steps.title: Change the implementation
steps.explanation: FlashAttention reorganizes exact attention around GPU memory traffic. An implementation improvement is a different kind of connection from a new architecture.

steps.title: End with an open question
steps.explanation: Which data regimes favor deep tabular models over trees? The map records a research question. A nearby paper or missing edge cannot prove a new combination will work.
